setup.title: Setup
setup.welcome_body: This wizard sets up your local knowledge server. Once configured, users connect to your Wi-Fi hotspot and open any browser. No internet needed.
setup.hardware_body: any Windows 10/11 PC works for Wikipedia, Gutenberg, and maps. Planning to add the offline chat assistant too? Budget about 5GB free disk. Also budget 8GB or more RAM for the recommended model. The largest option wants 16GB or more RAM. Each option on the Assistant tab lists its own requirement.
setup.hotspot_meaning_body: turning it on makes this PC act like a Wi-Fi router. Students connect using the network name and password you set on the Finish Setup tab. That's the same as joining any other Wi-Fi. No school network or router is involved. Students never need their own internet.
setup.safe_to_leave_label: It's safe to walk away mid-setup:
setup.safe_to_leave_body: downloads you start on the tabs above keep running in the background. This continues even if you close this browser tab. Reopening the app brings you right back to this page until you click {finish}. Nothing you've already downloaded is lost.
setup.getting_started_body: Content (Quick Start / Offline Assistant / Offline Maps) is entirely optional right now. Every tab above works the same way later from the Modules page. Feel free to skip straight to {finish} and add content afterward instead.
setup.admin_password_body: Used to reach this Admin panel later. Choose something only staff know.

services.subtitle: Everything runs in one process. No separate servers to start or crash. "Unload" just frees the in-memory handle. It reopens automatically on next use.

settings.export_diagnostics_body: Downloads a zip with the log file, settings (passwords excluded), and installed-module list. Handy to email whoever's helping you troubleshoot.
help.heading: Help & Troubleshooting
help.subtitle: Plain-language answers for the questions that come up most when running this on-site.
help.what_is_module_a: A module is one piece of content: Wikipedia, a map, the offline chat assistant. Each one is a self-contained folder under C:\OfflineHub\modules\. Installing one downloads it and adds it to the student portal automatically. Removing one (from the {modules_link} page) deletes just that folder and nothing else. There's no limit on how many you install beyond your PC's disk space.
help.what_is_hotspot_a: Turning on the hotspot makes this PC act like a Wi-Fi router. Student phones, laptops, and tablets connect using the network name (SSID) and password. You set both on the {hotspot_link} page. That's the same as joining any other Wi-Fi. No school router, internet connection, or extra hardware is involved. Once connected, opening any browser reaches the portal. Just go to this PC's address, shown on the Hotspot page. Students never need their own internet access.
help.admin_rights_a: Windows only allows starting a Wi-Fi hotspot from an elevated process. Close the app, then right-click OfflineHub.exe (or its shortcut). Choose "Run as administrator", and try again from the Hotspot page.
help.no_internet_a: This is the single most confusing part of running an "offline" app. Windows' built-in Mobile Hotspot needs this PC to already have some active network connection first. That can be Wi-Fi or Ethernet, even one with no real internet behind it. This PC needs a connection to share from. That's a Windows requirement, not something OfflineHub controls. Connect this PC to any network once. Even a phone's hotspot works for this. Then try starting the hotspot again. Students still won't need that connection once the hotspot is running.
help.netsh_error_q: It fails with a netsh / "hosted network" error
help.netsh_error_a: Some Wi-Fi adapter drivers don't support the older "hosted network" method at all. This is a driver limitation, not something adjustable in software. Open a Command Prompt and run netsh wlan show drivers. If "Hosted network supported" says No, this hardware can't use that method. Use the modern Mobile Hotspot path instead (see above).
help.download_fails_intro: A failed download shows a plain-English reason. Maybe not enough disk space, a network error, or a corrupted file. The button then turns into Retry. Click it to try again. Downloads resume from where they left off instead of starting over. If it keeps failing:
help.download_fails_disk_space: Check this PC has enough free disk space. Large items like maps and the offline assistant need several GB.
help.download_fails_connection: Check this PC's own internet connection. It's only needed while downloading, never for students afterward.
help.download_fails_retry_later: Try again later. The content is served by Kiwix's free public library, which occasionally has its own outages.
help.something_else_body: The {settings_link} page has an Export Diagnostics button. It zips up the log file and your settings, with passwords removed. It also includes the list of installed modules. Everything lands in one file you can email to whoever's helping you. Logs also live directly at C:\OfflineHub\logs\offlinehub.log if you want to look yourself.
